label: Early-sequence input of a token in a fixed set (t=0: e,h,p,s,2,b,v,x,t,k,u,o; t=1-2: mainly e,h,p,s)
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires almost only in the first three original-phase steps (t=0..2 hold 99% of the activation mass). It is never active at the delimiter and almost never active later in the original phase or in the copy phase. At t=0 it is an exact token detector: it fires on every one of 12 tokens (e,h,p,s,2,b,v,x,t,k,u,o) and on no other token (precision 1.0). At t=1-2 it fires dependably on e, h, p, s and only sometimes on the other set tokens, depending on context; it rarely fires once a set token has already appeared. Magnitude is largest for e (about 0.46 of max at t=0, up to 0.65 at t=1-2 after tokens like k c / k q), then h, p, s; digits and o, u are weak. A small tail (about 1% of mass) fires at copy step t=4 when L=3 and a set token is fed back (e.g. e a n <DEL> e gives the maximum activation).

issues: The t=0 claims hold: precision 1.0 on test, recall 0.62, 65% of activation mass. The timing claims also hold: t=0..2 carry 99% of the mass, the unit never fires at <DEL>, and the copy tail at t=4 is about 1% of mass.

The claim that it 'fires dependably on e, h, p, s at t=1-2' is false. Precision of that clause is 0.55 on test. By token: e 0.89, h 0.47, p 0.44, s 0.42. At t=2 the clause has precision 0.42, so h/p/s fire less than half the time. This clause produces most of the 11.9k test false positives (e.g. 'm 2 *p*', 'n *h* 0', 'l *s* w').

The claim that it 'rarely fires once a set token has already appeared' is not supported. For e/h/p/s at t=1-2, precision is 0.50 when a set token was seen earlier and 0.61 when none was. Adding ~seen(SET) to the predicate makes it worse (F1 0.743).

Missed activations at t=1-2 on other set tokens (b, u, o, 2, x, v) are systematic and depend on context: they fire more after c/q/y (precision 0.73 with prev in c,q,y, versus 0.21-0.34 per token overall). The label mentions this context dependence only vaguely.
A simpler predicate does better on test: t=0 set tokens, plus t=1 on e/h/p/s, plus t=2 on e only, gives F1 0.855 (P 0.913, R 0.803).
skeptic.revised_label: First-token detector for a fixed set of 12 tokens (e,h,p,s,2,b,v,x,t,k,u,o) at t=0 (exact). It fires weaker and context-dependently on the same tokens at t=1-2: reliably only for e, and about half the time for h/p/s, boosted when the previous token is c, q or y.
